Two ICES workshops on geo-spatial data for small-scale fisheries:

- **G1:** WKSSFGEO, Lisbon, 2021 (ICES Scientific Reports 4:10, [doi 10.17895/ices.pub.10032](https://doi.org/10.17895/ices.pub.10032));
  code and data at [ices-eg/WKSSFGEO](https://github.com/ices-eg/WKSSFGEO).
- **G2:** WKSSFGEO2, Faro, 2023 (ICES Scientific Reports 5:49, [doi 10.17895/ices.pub.22789475](https://doi.org/10.17895/ices.pub.22789475));
  code and data at [ices-eg/WKSSFGEO2](https://github.com/ices-eg/WKSSFGEO2).

What they ask for, and where each piece now is (ramb, fishymodel, iapesca, the ICES data call, others, or nowhere),
is in [One flow: what exists, and where](one_flow.qmd#what-exists). This page holds the workshops' example data and
the summary of the two reports.

## The example data, and which are in ramb

"In ramb" means a table in ramb's `inst/extdata`, read with `rb_read_example()`. "Not public" means the set was never on
either GitHub repository.

**Where the sets that are not public are.** The report itself names the place. Annex 5, the output of the script that
standardised the sets, finds them in three places: the WKSSFGEO GitHub (`data-examples/`), the WKSSFGEO2 GitHub, and
the **WKSSFGEO2 SharePoint**: `community.ices.dk/ExpertGroups/WKSSFGEO2`, folder `2022 Meeting Documents/06. Data`.
Section 2.3 says that script, `WKSSFGEO2_examples_data_base.Rmd`, is on the SharePoint "for workshop members" and on
the WKSSFGEO2 GitHub "for anyone"; the GitHub repository has neither the script nor these five sets (checked
2026-10-19, at f3e49fe). The report's summary calls the data set "openly available on ICES github", which holds for
only part of it.

The SharePoint is for WKSSFGEO2's members. The maintainer took part in WKSSFGEO, not WKSSFGEO2, but has access
(2026-10-19). The site runs SharePoint Server 2016, which downloads one file at a time and has no zip, so the sets are
not copied out yet (TODO 93). Whether a set may then go into ramb is for its provider to say.

Found beyond the workshops (decision 148), in `$FISHYDATA/raw/external/`, not in ramb:
- CNR-IRBIM's labelled tracks (Lattanzi et al. 2026, SoftwareX): 5 passive-gear vessels, 846 trips, 30 s.
- CNR-IRBIM's tracker log (Pulcinella et al. 2022, Sensors): one vessel, with power and geofence events.
- Mendo et al. 2023's soak-time code and samples.

Which of these go into ramb is TODO 93.

Not obtainable (decision 148): Timor-Leste's tracks from Peskas (WorldFish). About 350 small boats have carried GPS
trackers from Pelagic Data Systems since 2018, and there is no AIS. Only the landings are public. Peskas' code is
read in decision 231.

## Checked against the code (2026-10-19)

- CNR's `create_fishing_trip()` as coded (WKSSFGEO `dev_branch` efd28a8) differs from its own description in the
  report and in its release note:
  - a vessel is in port after 4 consecutive pings inside the port polygon at a mean speed under 6 kn;
  - a silence of over 4 h at sea, not 30 min, ends a trip;
  - split trips are joined unless both ends lie in the coastal zone, and then only if the joined trip lasts under 24 h;
  - `closest_port_recovery` takes the other end's port if it is among the 5 closest within 50 km, else the closest,
    else "At_Sea";
  - the port buffer is 0.001 degrees, with s2 off.

  ramb's `rb_create_voyages(method = "cnr")` reproduces the code trip for trip.
- The 94 CNR trips on the Danish data (G1 Annex 3) come from one call over all vessels together, which the function
  sorts by time alone. Per vessel, the same code gives 90.
:::

## Summary of the two reports

The two reports, summarised for a trip finder and for a full fishing-activity flow.

Both reports read in full. Pages are printed page numbers. G1 = WKSSFGEO (ICES Sci. Rep. 4:10); G2 = WKSSFGEO2 (5:49). G2 Annex 5, the data-standardising Rmd output after p. 87, has no page numbers: cited "A5". Presentation abstracts are folded into the sections where they hold a method or a number.

### 1. What each report is

- G1: 29 Nov-3 Dec 2021, IPMA Lisbon, hybrid; chairs Rufino, Egekvist (p. iii). ToR a: methods to identify trips/hauls in SSF, passive gears included; b: an R template script; c: how high-resolution data improve effort estimates (p. 1). 43 datasets (AIS 17, GPS 13, VMS 13), mostly 1 s-1 min, max 20 min (p. 5). Code at github ices-eg/WKSSFGEO (p. 35-38): DTU define_trips_pol (Jeppe Olsen); Irish trip method and potter HMM (Guillermo Martin, Marine Institute); CNR create_fishing_trip and classification_wrapper (Galdelli, Pulcinella, Tassetti); French features and RF toy (Danhiez); interpolation and downsampling (Jeppe/Niels, vmstools); an "Icelandic approach" HMM (Einar). Annex 3: CNR finder vs jepol (p. 47-57). Annex 4: review (p. 58-60).
- G2: 13-16 March 2023, Faro, hybrid, 38 participants; chairs Rufino, Mendo (p. iii). ToR a.i open anonymised example data; a.ii compare classification methods; a.iii ping rate by gear; b SSF coverage in ICES VMS/logbook, FDI, GFW; c guidance on tracking small vessels (p. 78). Funded by a DG ENV request (p. 79).
- Abstracts with no method or number, one line: GFW matches Sentinel radar detections to AIS to find dark vessels (G2 p. 4-5); NOAA AccessAIS (p. 7); ABIOMMED trawl bioeconomics (p. 7); Balearic green boxes (G1 p. 10); a Greek multi-criteria fishing-pressure index (G1 p. 11).

### 2. Terminology (G1 Table 3.1, p. 12-16)

- High-resolution: a fix at least every 15 min (p. 12).
- Fishing trip (EU 404/2011): "any voyage ... during which fishing activities are conducted", port to port; several a day each count (p. 13). The legal trip needs fishing.
- Days at sea: any 24 h or part absent from port; a 2 h SSF trip counts as a day (p. 12).
- Fishing day: proposed "Any day at sea with a fishing operation" (p. 13).
- Fishing event: haul or passive-gear use, in logbook terms; tracks show events logbooks ignore (damaged gear) (p. 14). Fishing operation: searching, set, soak, haul; "may include no fishing events" (p. 14).
- Haul: retrieval, end of an event. Set: placement, start of an event; also a string of passive gear (p. 14).
- Fishing time (404/2011): sea hours minus transit, dodging, idling, repair; for static gear vessel time or soak is unclear (p. 14). Soak time: set of each unit to start of its removal; start and end undefined (p. 15).
- Home port; base port (where a unit operates from, may be seasonal); landing site; "boat parking areas" where a vessel is berthed, moored or launched; some SSF leave from beaches (p. 16).
- Ping rate is not defined; G2 says a 30 s acquisition gives a 1 min interval, unexplained (p. 39).

### 3. Trip identification

G1 Table 4.2 (p. 20): leave/enter a harbour polygon (define_trips_pol); unlisted hotspots treated as harbours; for vessels not harbour-based, a coastline buffer; or a stop outside harbour/coast longer than e.g. 3 h ("varies with the fishery") starts a new trip; some split on the interval between pings (fits daily trips). Limits: beach departures, AIS switched on only outside harbour, drawing the polygon. Without logbooks, find fishing events first and group them into trips (p. 21); static gear may be set on one trip and hauled on another (p. 59).
Harbours (Table 4.1, p. 19): polygons; vmstools pointInHarbour (~1 NM buffer); hotspots from position frequency (RANN::nn2); a depth cut; buffer size from points in port; fishing within ~10 m of shore causes false positives.
Methods in G1 Table 5.5 (p. 37):

- Danish (Olsen, DTU): out of and back into harbour polygons; large gaps split a trip; tested on 10 s video-validated EM, GN/OT. Has a minimum and maximum duration, yet its defaults gave trips over the maximum; runs in under 1 min (p. 57).
- Irish (Martin): a trip is consecutive pings out of harbour (pointInHarbour, sortTacsat); iVMS 5 min, HMD. The potter HMM cuts trips internally (p. 38).
- Italian: create_fishing_trip, AIS 5 min (below).

G2:

- CNR ARGOS (p. 20-21): trip ends from zero-satellite/zero-power pings at device boot, with a minimum interval between shutdown and restart; a stop over 45 min starts a new trip; Teltonika 1 min; hauler sensor; code github irbimMAPS/ssf.
- Mendo et al.: automatic mooring-site detection where no port list exists (p. 6); IPMA wants ports without hand-drawn polygons (p. 3, 24).
- Daily trips: Alboran green boxes, ~100 vessels, ~9,000 one-day trips in 2021 (p. 3); Basque trips = days in AIS and sales notes (p. 6).
- The ping rate must catch short turnarounds between trips (p. 39).

#### CNR create_fishing_trip (G1 Annex 3, Pulcinella, Galdelli, Tassetti, 10/12/2021)

- Rule: points from leaving port to return; stores departure/arrival port, country, statistical area. Built for terrestrial AIS, large-scale, mainly trawl (p. 47).
- Gaps: "loss of signal of at least 30 minutes" spoils port assignment. Recovery: overlays trip end/start points on the coastal ban zone, compares ids and times, and joins with the nearest port if end and start "are consecutive, have a temporal distance shorter than 24 h and at least one is outside the coastal_ban_zone". Then closest_port_recovery forces a port "under other conditions", not given (p. 47).
- A sliding window of 3-6 pings; no minimum or maximum duration; no interpolation; cleaned pings; rebuilds trips across gaps and when the last fixes are not in harbour (p. 56-57).
- Layers: ICES + Mediterranean ports merged, Portugal missing (p. 49); ban zone = 3 nm buffer for northern Europe, made in QGIS, or the Mediterranean trawl ban, 3 nm or 50 m isobath (p. 47, 50). Port buffer st_buffer(ports, 0.001) on EPSG:4326, no unit stated (p. 49).
- Run on G1 example_data_AIS (p. 48). EX_1: 3 trips both, starts within ~4 min; jepol 3.09, 1.24, 5.63 h (p. 51-52). Whole set ~5 min vs under 1 min (p. 57). Equal counts on 8 of 12 vessels; CNR more on EX_10 (14 v 12), EX_3 (18 v 17), EX_7 (8 v 6), fewer on EX_9 (2 v 3) (p. 53-54). Equal counts hide errors: EX_11 26 v 26 but mean 102.5 h v 12.2 h. Matching, jepol as reference: one overlapping CNR trip within +/-10% of duration (p. 55). The 13 mismatch rows include CNR trips of 2,400 h and 811 h that failed to split, and jepol trips of 688 h and 6,301 h (p. 55-56). "Errors in both"; not analysed further (p. 56).
- Limits: renamed columns and new layers outside the Mediterranean; passive gear (8h); no run on Portuguese example_data_GPS, no harbours (p. 57).

### 4. Example data sets

G1 (github ices-eg/WKSSFGEO, data-examples):

- example_data_AIS: provider not named; columns vessel_id (EX_n), time_stamp, lon, lat, speed, course, gear, behaviour; rows 10 s apart; Oresund; trips 2013-2020; EX_5 and EX_8 absent from the comparison (p. 48, 53-56). G1's ML example used a DTU subset "including validated fishing operations" (p. 22), not said to be this file.
- example_data_GPS (Portugal): only named as unusable for CNR (p. 57). Scottish creels: a case study, no file (p. 31-32).

G2 template (p. 11-12): FILE_NAME, SOURCE, BOAT_ID, TRIP_ID, DATE_TIME (UTC), LATITUDE, LONGITUDE (4326), GEAR (ICES), PASSIVE_ACTIVE, STATUS (passive: setting/hauling/not_fishing; active: fishing/not_fishing); optional SPEED, COURSE, HEADING, QUALITY. Trips are given, not derived. Table 1 (p. 13-17) and A5, as provider; gear; area; period; interval; points/trips/vessels; labels; anonymised:

- DK_DTU_1897_EM: DTU; GNS; N Sea, Baltic ("Black Sea" also listed); dates shifted to 1897-98; 10 s; 879,053/284/5; EM, all trips; names, positions, times.
- ES_AZT_2018_AIS: AZTI; LLS, LTL, LHM, GXX; Biscay; 2018 shown as 1974-75; 60 s; 163,882/605/7; expert visual, "errors can occur"; satellite AIS linked to sales notes; names, positions, times. Not in A5.
- ES_IEO_2021_GRB: IEO; DRB, GNS, LLS, FPO, GTR; W Mediterranean; 1-2/2021; 180 s green box; 192,612/2,326 (3,326 "validated")/73; only DRB validated (27 boats, 373 trips, A5); names; A5 shows 11,882 negative intervals.
- FR_IFR_2021_GP: Ifremer (RECOPESCA); nets; English Channel (A5); 12/2021-1/2022; 900 s; 1,937/8/1; fisher's net positions and times; identity changed, positions "randomly translated" (A5); in iapesca.
- IE_MII_2019_IVMS: Marine Institute; HMD; Celtic Seas; 1/2019; 300 s; 2,094/8/6; validated visually only, "Could be wrong"; names, positions, times.
- IR_MII_2020_IVMS: Marine Institute; FPO; Celtic Seas; 2020; 60 s; 322/6/1; no validation.
- IT_CNR_2023_GP (Adriatic potter): CNR-IRBIM; FPO; 1-2/2023; 60 s Teltonika; 3,699/14/1; fisher interviews; names, positions, times; A5 table mislabelled "IE_MII_2019_IVMS"; 44 zero intervals.
- PT_CCM_2021_GP: CCMAR; FPO (octopus); Iberian; 9/2021-2/2022; 20 s portable GPS; 10,667/5 (7 on p. 27 and in A5)/3; experts + observers, setting/hauling; names; A5 intervals of -40 s (2,481) and 80 s (1,068).
- PT_IPM_2017_GP: IPMA; 4 DRB + 4 FPO trips; Iberian; 3/2017; 30 s; 9,115/8/8; expert visual; names and times, not positions.
- UK_USA_2018_GP (Scottish creels): St Andrews; FPO; 3-5/2018; 60 s portable GPS; 2,226/5/5; on-board observers.

Stated as 9 case studies (p. ii) or 10 (p. 72). Not in either report: "datatest", "IRL_FPO", "IRL_KY22". Irish tangle nets (crayfish, iVMS 10 min, observers) appear only in Table 2 (p. 21).

### 5. Validation numbers

- Trip finders: only the CNR-jepol comparison. Neither report scores a trip finder against labelled trips.
- Fishing activity: section 10. Linkage: Alboran green boxes to sales notes, 55% of trips (2021, p. 4); Basque sales notes to AIS trips, 55% (2018, p. 6).
- Measures (G1 p. 22-25): accuracy, kappa, F-score; RMSD, MRAD, bias, per-ping false positives/negatives; point-density skewness and kurtosis; plausibility (a "haul" shorter than the gear is wrong). Labels: expert-labelled tracks (cheap, need QC), logbooks, observers (costly), sensors. Validate few vessels over a full run of trips (p. 25).

### 6. Ping rate, headline

VMS's 2 h exceeds many SSF trips; SSF needs seconds to minutes (G1 p. 3, 39). G2 recommends 30 s acquisition (1 min interval) for every metier (p. 39, 72), but reports no results from its ping-rate framework (p. 37). Detail in 12.

### 7. Conclusions for a trip finder and port lists

- Port lists are incomplete (G1 p. 49, 57); include beaches and parking areas (p. 16, 28) or estimate harbours from the data (p. 19; G2 p. 6, 24). The legal trip requires fishing (p. 13).
- Gaps depend on the device: AIS can be switched off and has ~50 nm terrestrial range (G2 p. 43, 66); iVMS and green boxes store and forward (p. 9, 70); Irish units ping less inside port geofences (G1 p. 7). Trips can be multi-gear (G2 p. 1); no method fits all (p. 72).

### 8. Checks of the CNR rules as first read for plan 031

- **(a)** Not addressed. Annex 3 has only a 3-6 ping sliding window (p. 56-57); no 4-ping or 6 kn rule. The only 6 kn is IPMA's post-classification cap (G2 p. 3).
- **(b)** Half confirmed: the code is st_buffer(ports, 0.001) on EPSG:4326 (p. 49); "1 km" is not in the report. My inference, not the report's: with sf >= 1.0 and s2 on, the distance on lon/lat is in metres, so 0.001 means ~0.001 degree (~110 m) or 1 mm depending on the session.
- **(c)** Not confirmed: a gap is "loss of signal of at least 30 minutes" (p. 47); no 4 h rule.
- **(d)** Partly contradicted: the report states the release-note rule, join if consecutive, under 24 h from end to next start, and at least one end outside the zone (p. 47). "Not both in the zone" agrees; the 24 h is a gap, not a combined duration.
- **(e)** Not addressed: closest_port_recovery is only named (p. 47); no 50 km, 5 ports, "At_Sea".
- **(f)** Confirmed by summing the per-vessel table: 94 vs 90 over 12 vessels (p. 53-54). The report gives no totals, only 8/12 equal.
- **(g)** Not addressed: the Irish method is consecutive pings out of harbour (G1 p. 37), no gap rule. Nearest: the Irish tangle-net HMM drops trips with pings over 5 min apart (G2 p. 21).
- **(h)** Confirmed (p. 47); the stated reason is that it "does not require at least one fishing event during the trip".

### 9. Preprocessing (G1 Table 4.1, p. 17-20; p. 35-36)

- UTM if the extent is under 5 degrees, else haversine; sf, not sp; prefilter big files (p. 17). Time zones, future points (p. 18).
- Speed: threshold, percentile, moving average; compare reported with computed speed (p. 18).
- Duplicates: vessel + time (+ position), 2 s buffer (p. 18). Land: shapefiles or own polygons (p. 18-19).
- Interpolation: linear, COG+speed curves (vmstools interpolateTacsat), Kalman, ML; limit interpolated points; uneven sampling may bias models (p. 19). DTU splines gaps to 1 per minute (p. 9). Fails for circling gear (G2 p. 40); French ML needs linear resampling (G2 p. 4).
- Downsampling: mean or nearest, e.g. 5 min; a sensitivity protocol suggested (p. 19-20, 36). Post-process: re-check land and outliers, recompute variables (p. 20).
- Vessel id from MMSI or call sign via the register, or from the AIS name (DTU, p. 9).
- G2: standardising script WKSSFGEO2_examples_data_base.Rmd (p. 12); irregular green-box gaps (p. 3); keep 4-5 decimals (p. 65).

### 10. Methods to infer fishing activity

G1 Table 4.3 (p. 21): speed filter + turning angle, HMM, EM, RF, XGBoost, CNN, C5.0. Pitfall: slowing without fishing (approach, cleaning nets) (p. 9, 21). Active gear: a speed band with typical geometry; passive: set, soak, haul (p. 21). Variables (p. 26, 36): time of day, speed, turning, acceleration, jerk, sinuosity, depth, substrate, season, tide, gear rules, vessel. Chain gear, then fishing, then gear size; handle NAs; balance classes (p. 26-27).

- Speed rules: North Irish Sea HMD, iVMS 10 min, plus a <~12 m depth buffer (G1 p. 31). Greece: OTB <=4 kn, PS <=1 kn on interpolated VMS, no validation (G2 p. 22-23). Basque bands from fishers: passive set/haul 0-1 kn, trolling 6-7 kn, AIS 1 min (p. 6, 21). Irish tangle nets, 10 min (p. 21).
- Threshold vs Gaussian mixture (EM), overall or per trip: Scottish creels (60 s, observers): per-trip mixture best and fastest; one overall rule fails across regions and sizes (G2 p. 19). CCMAR octopus (20 s): 74% accuracy, precision 63% vs 64% per trip; not_fishing missed (p. 27). French nets: 49.12%; per-trip binary clustering 64.94% (p. 32).
- HMM: Irish iVMS potter/HMD on step and angle, states Fishing, Transit, Mix_Transit, initial values per boat, extended to 10 min; on G2 datasets agreement "varied substantially", judged visually (G2 p. 19-20, 29). French: speed 42.60%, speed + angle 50.00% (p. 32). Uses sequence, but complex and slow (p. 26).
- RF and ML: Scottish RF (speed, angle, share of trip elapsed) 94% (p. 19, 26). IPMA dredges + octopus, 170 tracks: RF, boosting >95%; 10% training (17 trips) 80-96%; best at raw 30 s; 10-point speed average; k-neighbour smoothing and no fishing above 6 kn give RF 99.07% (p. 2-3, 26). IEO longlines RF, AIS ~3 min; observers' set/haul times imprecise (p. 23-24). RECOPESCA gear class: XGBoost 94.89%, 25,612 trips, 107 vessels, 34 trip features (G1 p. 6-7). DTU workshop example "not satisfying" (G1 p. 22). ML ignores sequence (G2 p. 26).
- French netters (iapesca), 8 trips, 15 min: CART and RF 91.5% (3-fold CV by trip), poor on sets; RF + geocomputation 94.3% (nets built from hauls, sets retrieved by buffers and scored candidates). Waiting on the grounds reads as hauling (G2 p. 30-36).
- Others: CNR cascade per trip, OTB/PTM/TBB/PS, untested (G1 p. 38); hauler sensors (G2 p. 1, 20); four passive states incl. drift for soak (G2 p. 5); VMS-AIS fusion and LSTM (p. 23); neural networks proposed (p. 26-27).

### 11. Effort indicators (G1 Table 4.6, p. 27-30)

- Days at sea: trips only; report hours at sea instead (p. 27).
- Hours fished: mobile = inferred fishing; static = soak, set at t to haul at t+y, maybe another trip (p. 27). Fishing days likewise (p. 27-28).
- kW or GT x days at sea or fishing days: register, keyed on the EU CFR; SSF registers unreliable (p. 28). kW-hours not defined.
- Fishing operations: count hauls if sets are invisible; three-level indicator (set+haul, haul only, set only) (p. 28-29).
- Net length = distance of pings classed as hauling; soak from overlapping set and haul tracks; hooks and pots via observed spacing (p. 29-30).
- Swept area: gear-width polygons for mobile bottom gear (DTU, p. 9).
- Day measures overstate SSF effort; soak from start, middle or end is unsettled (p. 30). For passive gear, track length beats time at sea (G2 p. 5).

Case studies: North Irish Sea razor clams, all <12 m, 10 min, hours fished by speed and depth (G1 p. 31). Scottish traps: hauls inferred, creel numbers from hauled distance with 95% CI (p. 31-32). South Portugal octopus: ~60 trackers, observers label set/haul (p. 33). Portuguese dredges: 80 vessels, 5.45-15.82 m, 2,100-2,700 t (2018-2020), 3-15 m deep in the south, to 34 m in the northwest, ~30 s with operation status (p. 33-34). French netters: 39 nets, 398.8 km observed vs 37, 362.3 km predicted; 7 of 8 trips consistent (G2 p. 32, 35).

### 12. Ping rate against gear

- Trammel shooting can be under 20 min, missed at low rates; sensors compensate (G1 p. 24). Net length needs a sufficient rate (p. 40).
- French nets: 15 min gives degraded but consistent fishing hours; sets, hauls, soak and net length need 1 min (SSF) or 2 min (>15 m) (G2 p. 4).
- IPMA: 30 s to 10 min tested, best at 30 s (p. 2). Irish HMM: trouble above 10 min (p. 20); crayfish HMM <=5 min (p. 21). RECOPESCA: gear class at <=15 min (G1 p. 7).
- What sets the rate (G2 p. 39): trip and event durations, trips per day, track complexity, events per trip (coarse rates merge them), set/haul overlap for soak. Rule: shortest trip / points needed, 2 h / 50 = 3.6 min (p. 40). At 2 h, 25 kn covers 90 km, 2 kn 7 km (p. 42).

### 13. Data sources (G2 sec. 5, p. 41-67)

- ICES VMS/logbook: logbooks >10 m (>8 m Baltic), ICES rectangle only; VMS >12 m since 2012, 2 h, no activity flag; national activity rules may count port and passage as fishing; monthly, 0.05 degree c-squares; VMSenabled flag (p. 41-42). Portugal and Lithuania logbooks dropped, Norway and Iceland excluded (p. 43).
- FDI: SSF without logbooks from declarations, sales notes or surveys, one sale note = one fishing day (p. 43, 57); 12-18 m class, no 15 m split (p. 44); no UK for 2021 (p. 56).
- GFW AIS: class A >15 m since 2014; nearly all EU >15 m in the Mediterranean, but gillnetters and longliners missed; EU register only; GFW gear classes (p. 43-44). Series ICES 2009-2021, FDI 2013-2021, GFW 2016-2021 (p. 44).
- Findings: passive gears dominate effort; ~1/3 of area 27 is mobile bottom gear (MBCG) (p. 64); AIS days rise 2016-2021, mostly 12-15 m (p. 47); 10-12 m VMS trawling on the slope suggests misclassification (p. 57).
- FDI MBCG 2021 (Annex 4, p. 84-87): area 27, <12 m 235,531 vs >12 m 303,964 days (44%); 27.9.a 82%; Mediterranean 76,091 vs 449,469 (14%), miscaptioned "FAO area 27".
- MBCG days 2021, AIS / logbook / FDI (Annex 3, p. 80-83), my sums: <10 m 8,656 / 16,200 / 24,224; 10-12 m 18,604 / 30,320 / 35,488; 12-15 m (FDI 12-18) 62,983 / 24,770 / 71,829. 27.9.a <10 m: 0 / 3 / 9,703. "Difficult to compare" (p. 56, 64).
- Danish positions cover, by landed value, >91% of trawls/seines but 3-20% of pots (2015-2020, G1 p. 9).

### 14. Tracking small vessels

- VMS >=12 m at 2 h, with an exemption for 12-15 m vessels in territorial waters or on trips under 24 h (G2 p. 78); AIS >=15 m; logbooks >=10 m; tracking of all vessels proposed in 2018, still negotiated (G1 p. 3-4; G2 p. 68-69). Schemes: Portugal 150 boxes at 30 s (G2 p. 2), Andalucia since 2004 at 3 min (p. 3), Ireland razor-clam iVMS (G1 p. 7), England and Wales iVMS mandatory 2023 (G2 p. 68, 70).
- Options (G2 p. 65-66): simple electronic logbooks; GPS with a start/end button; VMS for all, via GSM; AIS (status 7 "engaged in fishing", can be switched off).
- Challenges: cost, phasing, formats, duplicate reporting, mistrust, power at high latitude in winter (p. 66, 69).

### 15. Anonymising tracks

G2 data may hide positions, times and ids, with a script (p. ii, 8); the form records which (p. 10). Seen: replaced ids, shifted dates (DK to 1897, AZTI to 1974), randomly translated positions (FR, A5); the script's method is not described. Public AIS exposes grounds to competitors (G2 p. 9). A data call would be anonymised and aggregated (p. 70).

### For a trip-finder benchmark, beyond the above

- G2's labelled trips (TRIP_ID) as truth for daily fleets, resampled from 10 s to 15 min (Rufino_2023_ping_rate.Rmd; Fig. 3 uses 30 s-20 min, p. 37-38).
- Matching protocol: one overlap within +/-10% of duration, per-vessel count and mean and total duration, runtime (G1 p. 52-57).
- Robustness cases: negative and zero intervals, duplicates, store-and-forward bursts, AIS off near port, boot pings, beach launches, multi-gear trips, trips of hundreds of hours.
- Thresholds to sweep: 3 h and 45 min stops, 30 min gap, 24 h join, ~1 NM harbour buffer, 3 nm ban zone (section 3); port layers harbours.rds plus CNR's Mediterranean ports (G1 p. 47, 49).
- If this summary enters a report, mark it as AI-generated.
